newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian central banker sees no further gold sales.
newsitem.headline: Belgian central banker sees no further gold sales.

text.p: Belgian National Bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said in a newspaper interview that he was happy with the level of the central bank's gold reserves after sales in recent years and that there would be no further sales.
"After selling 700 tonnes, we have a gold reserve in line with the European average," he told La Libre Belgique.

He said G-10 central bankers had an accord not to destabilise the gold market and to ask each other for permission in the case of planned sales. "I have obtained that permission four times. I will not try for a fifth time," he said.
Verplaetse said the central banks estimated it was possible to sell the equivalent of one or two tonnes of gold a day without destabilising the market.
The G-10 consists of the U.S., Germany, Japan, Canada, the UK, France, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Sweden.
The interview with Verplaetse was in the context of Belgium's plan to use some 236 billion Belgian francs of foreign exchange reserves generated from gold sales to cut the national debt.
